utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Negodic. May I remind you of the affirmation you took at the beginning which still applies. Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Rodic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning to everyone. Mr. Negodic, tell me kindly: On the 6th of December, near the Libertas Hotel, did a member of the Croatian navy, Bruno Glanc, get killed?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the details. All I know is that two refugees and three fire-fighters who were putting out the fire at the hotel got killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any members of the Croatian National Guard, Home Guard, who got killed?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. As I said, they are divided into infantry battalions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday that hotels in Dubrovnik were used only to accommodate soldiers and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic --

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- to feed them? THE COURT: [Previous translation continues]... only in there, which I don't think reflects the evidence. As this was interpreted a moment ago, you said that hotels in Dubrovnik were used only to accommodate soldiers. That doesn't accord with the evidence we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I quoted yesterday's testimony of this witness, where the hotels -- where he said that hotels were used only for providing food. And since my question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... of the evidence of yesterday about food was that hotels were a convenient source of providing food, and therefore, they were used for that purpose, the hotel kitchens. It didn't move from there to the proposition you have put, that hotels in the Dubrovnik area were used only for -- to accommodate soldiers, which you put to the witness. There is a great body of evidence that the hotels were used to accommodate refugees, they were used to accommodate the European monitors, et cetera, media, and so on. So they had uses other than for the military purposes of the Croatian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was speaking only about military needs. I did not include the things that you are mentioning now. My question only referred to the standpoint of military needs. I asked whether the soldiers were accommodated in hotels, and the answer was negative. And then I said that from the point of view of military needs, the military only used the hotels to provide food for the troops. I am not going into other aspects of the use of the hotels.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: This may be some confusion introduced by the interpreter, who did not manage to finish the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the usher to help me distribute some documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we may have an explanation there of our discussion, Mr. Rodic. It seems that you moved too quickly for the interpreters, so what I read and heard was only a small part of what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are two documents which refer precisely to this issue of use of hotels for military needs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, would you kindly look at this document issued by the command of the sector defence of November. It was signed by Lieutenant Colonel Nojko Marinovic and it was addressed to the headquarters of the civilian defence of Dubrovnik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says that: "For the purposes of accommodation and providing food of members of the armed forces of the sector of Dubrovnik, no provision, no adequate provision, was made, and for that purpose, we order..." So the command of this sector orders; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Neptun, President, Vila Beograd, and Stadion shall continue to be used for these purposes. Are these the hotels?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Vila Beograd being a rest home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that members of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia were accommodated in these hotels?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Neptune -- more precisely, in one of the pavilions of the Neptune hotel, and the western side of the Stadion Hotel, where cooking was done for the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the President?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the President. It was used to accommodate refugees, and there was only the crew of the Maljutka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the Stadion Hotel?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a water polo playground, and that's why it was called Stadion. There were only a couple of rooms occupied by refugees.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Adriatic, Komodor, and the Ceska Vila used for the needs of the navy and the war refugees?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hotel Komodor was a command post for the HRN. Cooking was done there for the army, but it is not true of the Ceska Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it say also that other needs need to be specified, especially the quality of services provided to the armed forces? From this we see that hotels were also used to accommodate members of the armed forces of the Republic of Croatia, or are you going to deny this document issued by the commander?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not denying his document, but I gave you a clarification, which hotels were used. We have a lot of hotels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do not waste my time. You denied, in answer to my direct question, that members of the Croatian army were accommodated in hotels at all. That was your answer yesterday.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday you told me not to take up too much time. I'm only answering your specific questions. If you asked me -- if you had asked me if there were any hotels where accommodation was provided for the army, I would have told you which hotels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, we have a record and we can check this. Please look at this document dated 17th November, which the headquarters of civilian defence addressed to the command of the defence of Dubrovnik municipality. It was the commander of the headquarters Kreso Milas who wrote this document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it say that after the devastation of hotels Minceta, Plakir, and Tirena, these headquarters have the task to provide accommodation for 1.500 displaced persons elsewhere, 1.500 expelled persons elsewhere? That's in the introduction.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it say that, further on, that the headquarters of civilian defence request from the command to make room in at least one hotel where your forces are accommodated, provided that the facility is suitable for accommodating these expelled persons? In other words, is an appeal made to the command of civilian defence to give one of the hotels to the refugees, one of the hotels currently used by military forces?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's his request.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Is this the essence of the request?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like these two documents to be marked as Defence exhibits. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The one dated 17th of November will be D75. The one dated 9th of November will be D76.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, yesterday I was corrected once again, but I checked the record after that. During the first session, on Friday the 24th, you said that the crew commanded by Primic, Zoran Primic, was there on the 6th December. You said: "I know because I gave the orders. They were divided between two positions, SDK and 120 metres to the east of Old Town, to repel or prevent the attack from the site of Dubac." That was in lines 4 to 14 on page 4. That is what I repeated yesterday, this distance of 120 metres and the purpose of this position, Lazaret. Is it true that Lazaret is 100 metres east of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was its purpose to prevent an attack from the side of Dubac?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it was set up, this position had the main purpose of preventing an attack from the side of Dubac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. When you gave your statement to the investigators in December 2003, under paragraph 32 of your statement, which you later corrected - and I'm emphasising this - which you corrected before your examination-in-chief, in your original statement, you said: "When, at 11.30, they stopped firing from the position at Lazareti, four shells were left out of the total of 20 they had at the beginning of the day." When you corrected the statement, it read as follows: "At the position near the SDK, Dubrovkinja, at Gruz, they ran out of ammunition and two men went to the Lazaret position, which was not active on the 6th of December, to bring four shells that were available at that position." These two statements of yours, do they differ in essence?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how it was translated. All I know is that I said that at the beginning, at this firing position, there were 20 shells, all but four were used up, and after 11.30, men went to get those four remaining shells from that position, Lazaret.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: In relation to your original statement given in December 2003, did you mean to deny that there was activity from the Lazaret position? Because that position was near the Old Town. Answer me with yes or no.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer with a yes or no. I need to make a clarification.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You explained already. I'm asking you: Was your motivation, was your meaning to deny that there was action from this position?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 6th of December, no fire was opened from that position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it the case that four shells could, under any circumstances, be called a storage of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, because while giving evidence you pointed out that on the 6th of December you did go to this position by the SDK; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me at what time you were there, approximately?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They said that they were without any ammunition. They called at 11.30, and when I finished, as I already said, taking the wounded people to the hospital, I returned to the position. I did not find the commander and the deputy commander because they went to get those four shells. I don't know what else I'm supposed to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me: How long did you stay at that position by the SDK?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very briefly. The crew was in the atomic shelter. There was no need for them to be at the combat positions since they had no ammunition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go from that position by the SDK building before Zoran Primic and Zvonko Pilas returned?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you then about the four shells?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crew said that the commander and deputy commander went to get the four shells from the Lazaret position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is what the rest of the crew told you, the people you found there in that shelter?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. Not the rest of the crew, but the entire crew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what are Primic and Pilas, then?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you probably phrase your questions in such a way so that it would turn out that the rest of the crew is at the Lazareti position, but I already said that there were no crew members at the Lazareti position and that fire was not opened from there. So the entire crew was at the position by the SDK, except for the commander and the deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You still claim that Bogisica Park was used only one day during the defence of Dubrovnik from the 1st of October until the 31st of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to put the following to you, what your commander said, Nojko Marinovic, in the statement that he gave to the investigators, since he speaks otherwise --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I object. I don't know whether it is appropriate to put a statement made by another witness who is not even being called right now, this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you intending to call that witness, Mr. Rodic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You can go so far as to put to the witness whether he would agree with certain things. Where you get those from doesn't matter and should not be mentioned. The witness will either agree or not agree. You must accept his answer. That's as far as you can go at this point. Because you can't go further, you may not want to put it at all. It's up to you. But you can put a proposition to the witness whether that is correct or not correct. But if you're not going to call the witness, you shouldn't go into details about where you get the information from.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps we are ultimately going to call those witnesses. These are witnesses who were on the Prosecution list and the Prosecution gave up on them. What I am putting to the witness now is not evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, if you would just put the proposition, if you want to. I'm not stopping you doing that. Just don't ascribe it to a particular person or put a statement to -- show the witness the statement. You can quote a passage from it and say: Is this correct or is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, just for the record. The Prosecution did not give up on this witness, but due to his health conditions, is compelled to not to call at this particular stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, so let me check this once again. Although we had a different practice when Witness Jusic was giving evidence, now, in accordance with your instructions, I can only read out from the statement what I wish to put to the witness but without saying who it was who said it? Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, do you agree - I'm quoting something to you - Bogisica Park is 300 metres away from Pile Gate, towards the Old Town? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I think it's about 500 to 600 metres. Six hundred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "The weapons were as good as the shells that we got. At first we had JNA shells and instructions for exact calculations made regarding charges. Eventually we started getting Croatian shells, but not instructions for charging. So we were never sure --"

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. Counsel is reading verbatim from a statement which I think is not exactly Your Honour's ruling. Your Honour's ruling, as I understood, was that the proposition can be put to the witness and then get his comment on it, but right now counsel is reading verbatim the statement. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, it may appear to be a little confusing to you, but to try and assist you, especially in the early stages of this trial, I relaxed certain rules to try and help. In the interests of trying to ensure that we get through the important matters in the least of time, I am not continuing that relaxed position but bringing it back nearer to the true position. Now, what you might put to this witness, I would suggest, is a series of propositions. Just as examples: Is it true that Bogisica Park is only 300 metres from the Pile Gate? Is it true that you got Croatian shells at some time? Is it true that they didn't have instructions? Et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, is it correct that at first you only had JNA shells, and instructions for exactly calculating the charges?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Eventually, did you start getting Croatian shells, but you did not have instructions for charging them?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there some at some positions?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much at which positions?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because there were no instructions for charging the Croatian shells, is it a fact that you were never sure where a shell would fall?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are assumptions to that effect, but again, it could fall on the slopes of Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because of such conditions, did you have to fire many more shells just in order to engage a particular target?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If targeting is conducted with one type only, then not that many are necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the mortar crew have its base in Bogisica Park all the way up to May 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bogisica Park is about 200 square metres altogether. It has some pine trees. It is readily visible from Zarkovica. There was no base there. It was a one-off mortar position for the 82-millimetre mortar, and I've explained that several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But you are denying, or rather, you are saying in response to my question that until May 1992, there were no mortars in Bogisica Park; that's the point, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 6th of December, in the early evening hours, after the shooting abated, did anybody go back, or rather, did anybody go to Bogisica Park? Any members of your unit, I mean, any artillery men?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about any such details. I see no reason for anyone to go to that position, that particular place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Was there a warehouse with a few ammunition boxes, ammunition for mortars, near Ploce?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the Lazareti combat position?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I am referring to a place right by Ploce. Was there a warehouse there? Or, if it wasn't a warehouse, were boxes of mortar ammunition stored somewhere there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you, sir: The only warehouse for mortars was by the firing position of the SDK. That's a warehouse. And what you said at Ploce was actually Lazareti and there were shells underneath the steps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's not expand on that. We've heard about that already. Tell me: The commander and the deputy commander of the position by the SDK, Primic and Pilas, on the 6th of December did they bring a few boxes of ammunition from Ploce to the position at the SDK building?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no warehouse, there is no ammunition depot near Ploce or at Ploce.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were there any boxes with mortar ammunition at Ploce?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. There was only the Lazareti combat position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The mortars behind the SDK building, on the 6th of December, did they fire over 1.000 shells on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number because this was the decisive day when no economising was done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Zoran Primic, as commander of the mortar crew, did he receive orders in September 1991 to fire 82-millimetre mortar shells, 50 to 60 of them, at the village of Bani?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. There could be no shooting at the village of Bani because it was from Herzegovina and Montenegro that Bani were targeted. There was no need for our men to target their own area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the period between the 1st of October and the 31st of December, in Dubrovnik, or rather, under the control of the Dubrovnik forces, were there the following equipment: Four 85-millimetre guns; two ZIS anti-aircraft tanks; 10 anti-aircraft guns, three-barrelled, 20-millimetres; and two anti-aircraft guns, 20 millimetres but single-barrelled ones; two mortars of 120 millimetres; and two mortars of 82 millimetres; then six mortars of 82 millimetres -- the previous ones were in Brgat, and these six were in Cepikuce. Then two mortars of 82 millimetres and two 60-millimetre ones, positioned in Vodovodje. Three mortars of 82 millimetres in Bogisica Park, and two mortars of 120 millimetres at the auto camp at Babin Kuk in Dubrovnik? To the best of your knowledge, did these quantities of weapons ever exist in Dubrovnik and were they deployed at these places?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the things that you mentioned, sir, require time to be dealt with. Even a tape-recorder would need time to record all of that. These are different commands affecting different areas. As far as I can remember, I said yesterday, and I made a correction, and I know about my area; it wasn't four but it was two 82-millimetres mortars. As for all the rest, I simply don't know about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: In the period between mid-October and the end of December 1991, in the town of Dubrovnik itself, were the following deployed: One ZIS cannon at the end of Babin Kuk; three mortars of 120 millimetres near the parking lot at Babin Kuk; two cannons of 85 millimetres at Lapad; two ZIS cannons near the sport grounds by the Lero Hotel; one ZIS cannon on the Lapad peninsula, to the west of the Libertas Hotel; two anti-aircraft three-barrelled guns at Lapad, west of the Lero Hotel; and three 82-millimetre mortars in Bogisica Park to the west of the Imperijal Hotel?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. What I said already means that you can ask me to give an explanation about positions that existed then. But please, as regards such long questions, they are impossible to answer. I have stated several times that the quantities you keep referring to simply do not exist or were not there. Where they went from the area of Dubrovnik, I don't know. But the situation was not as you put it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these amounts that I read out to you for the period of mid-October until the 31st of December are not correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir; they're not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the usher's assistance, I would like the following document distributed. Your Honours, we received this document from the Prosecution in the course of cross-examination, so we did not have time to have it translated into English. With the help of this witness, I will ask two questions based on this document, and I believe that will help clarify. And we will provide an English translation in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, is this document issued by the command of the Dubrovnik municipality, dated 19 December, addressed to the operative zone Split?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says: "With the purpose of gaining an insight, we give you an overview herewith of the status of ammunition." And then goes a list of weapons and ammunition; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at the first weapon: "Cannon, 76-millimetres, ZIS, two pieces (without sights)."

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that situation -- was that the situation on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now look at the item referring to mortars of 82 millimetres, ten pieces.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain, in relation to those seven mortars of 72 [as interpreted] millimetres that you mentioned regarding the 6th of December, were there another three mortars supplied prior to the 19th December and provided to your forces?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And you can see that we were supplied with more ammunition as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Out of these ten mortars --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's a transcript error. It has gone down as 72 millimetres, but it should be 82 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, is it true that out of ten mortars, 82 millimetres, six lack sights?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly whether it was five or six.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this was signed by the commander, Nojko Marinovic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suppose that reports of this kind indicating the state of ammunition were drawn up after gathering data from subordinates.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would appreciate it if this document could be marked as a Defence exhibit as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of the usher, I would like to distribute another document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, you see here an overview of symbols designating certain weapons, artillery weapons, and military units. Can you tell me, if you look towards the bottom, the end, the circle with a black edge, it says Bitnica. What is Bitnica?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a battery.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can this symbol be used to designate a battery of cannons, a battery of mortars, a battery of other artillery pieces?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A battery is a general term for such a unit, if you can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me now, looking from the top: The fifth symbol from the top, the abbreviation is OBT. Does it mean coastal gun, 85 millimetres?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what they called it. It is a cannon dating back to the Second World War, which was used as an anti-aircraft gun and then became -- came to be used as a coastal weapon to be used against ships.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: Are there such guns in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the relevant period, no, not in the area of the Dubrovnik city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you mean this period, you mean the 6th of December or you mean the broader period?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The period we referred to several times, the 10th, 11th, and 12th month. There were no such guns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were no 85-millimetre cannons in that relevant period?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now look at the second symbol from the bottom [as interpreted], this arrow flanked by two dots.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's an anti-aircraft cannon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is the symbol for the anti-aircraft cannon. Was this symbol used on the P160 map that we discussed?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: There's a transcript error. It should be second symbol from the top, not from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. We'd managed to find it, but it was -- may be confusing for the future, so it is the second from the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this second symbol from the top, you interpreted it correctly, it was used to designate an anti-aircraft gun.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. That's what it says here as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the fact that it says here in this list, do you know that it is so?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the same symbol seen on the P160 map that we discussed yesterday? If you remember that sign to the north of the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the same symbol.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to ask that this document indicating symbols be also marked as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, before that, it might be appropriate to set a basis for this document. Of course, the witness has identified certain symbols, but as to what the source of this document is, et cetera, perhaps it might be appropriate to get that down on record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, it can be approached in two ways. Mr. Negodic, you've been asked to comment on some of the symbols that are on this document. Are the other symbols ones that you are familiar with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And are they correctly identified on this sheet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not familiar with the assault and landing ship item, but the rest that regards artillery weapons, yes, I'm familiar with these.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And which is the one you're not familiar with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The one that says Desantni Brod, assault and landing ship.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I can be of assistance, it is the fifth symbol from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Assault and landing ship.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I take it this is not a document that you prepared yourself, Mr. Negodic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a general document. I don't even know who wrote it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, can you recognise in this document the signature in the upper right corner?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be quite sure, but I think it could be Mr. Marinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document was disclosed to the Defence and it was drawn up by Nojko Marinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, it appears that it may be. But in answer to your objection, Ms. Mahindaratne, I think the witness has sufficiently confirmed the correctness of all but one item on the sheet, and as such, its relevance and assistance to the Chamber are sufficiently apparent to justify its reception.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, on the 6th of December, you were at the position of the ZIS cannon near the Ivo Vojnovic Street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: Why did you place the cannon under the bridge? Was it because you didn't want it to be noticed by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one of the reasons. Mostly it was for security reasons, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. safety reasons, because it was an earth surface.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You said that you fired 170 shells on that day.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around that number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, what did you target, which direction?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, the Srdj fortress, the Kriz or cross near the fortress, and the cable-car. To a lesser extent, Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do we then agree that the ZIS cannon is an anti-armour cannon?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Its function is both anti-armour and anti-infantry. It uses two kinds of ammunition. So if you use anti- -- if you use it as an anti-armour weapon, you use an appropriate kind of ammunition. It uses different shells when it targets infantry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it have a specific trajectory?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this case, because it shot, it fired directly at a small distance, at a close range.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What range?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to three kilometres. For a cannon that has a range of 13.5 kilometres, this is called direct shooting, at close range.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that this anti-armour tank, because it has a direct trajectory, cannot shoot over the old city, because it would hit it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot divert its trajectory. It shoots only directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, the 6th of December, how many shells in total did you have for the 82-millimetre mortar and the 120-millimetres mortars?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you that precisely. I already explained that after the 6th of December, I was in hospital, so I did not attend the meetings that discussed the total consumption of ammunition and nobody informed me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, when exactly did you go to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the night between the 6th and the 7th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before you went to the hospital, that is, before the beginning of action and combat on the 6th of December, did you know what quantity of ammunition for mortars was at your disposal in the defence of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I used to know, but now, after so many years, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But after so many years, you seem to remember very well that 20 shells and the four shells that you told us about regarding the Lazaret position.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was a special position which was active only once and that's why I remembered it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: How many shells were fired then from the mortar on the 6th of December, and from which positions?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said already, from the SDK position and the Babin Kuk position, shells were fired against three enemy positions, but I do not know how many shells were spent or indeed how many shells there were in the first place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us an approximate number?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dear sir, I really can't, even though I would like to help you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of artillery chief are you if you have no idea how many shells you had before action, how many you spent during the operation? Because you let us know during your testimony that you had good contact with your units and you controlled their positions and activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour -- I object to this line of questioning. It's inappropriate for counsel to make this type of derogatory statements against the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I agree it's unnecessary, but please go ahead, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As the person at the top who was responsible for artillery, do you make requests through your command for resupply of ammunition to your artillery?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got resupplies of ammunition little by little, by speedboat, in very small quantities. And in all that action, we did not have time to follow the proper written procedure. And now you're asking me, 13 years later, to remember exactly how much I asked for and when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, you said that on the 6th of December you were left with 10 per cent of ammunition for artillery weapons, after the completion of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me: 10 per cent of which quantity?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After I returned to the command, when I came back from the hospital, there was discussion to that effect at the command. And later, when I visited the positions, I was told that certain positions ran completely out of ammunition and others had 10 per cent left of the original amount.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then ask for a resupply?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As you could see from the document, there were two cases, either the 17th or the 19th of November [as interpreted], where it says 120 shells for the ZIS cannon, 76 millimetres, and some ammunition for the 82-millimetre mortar. That means that between the 6th and the 17th, or the 19th, some ammunition was provided for these weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you know, Mr. Negodic, if you did not --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's a transcript error. It has gone down as 17th or 19th of November. It should be December. The document related to December, as I recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, Mr. Negodic: On what basis did you then count the 170 shells fired from the ZIS cannon at the position near the Ivo Vojnovic Street?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said hello to the crew by the cannon, they told me: Mr. Ivan, we fired around 170.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the SDK crew?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The cannon crew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That much I understood. But what were you told by the crew of the mortars, near the SDK building?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that day, after 11.30, when I visited that position, I did not return to that position again. There was no need for me to go there. I only asked about people wounded. They told me that they went to get four shells. I didn't see any reason to discuss the consumption of shells at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Zoran Primic tell you that he had gone to get the missing shells for mortars at the position near the SDK through the Old Town to bring them back?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crew told me that Primic had gone to get them. It wasn't he who told me so, because when I came there, he wasn't at the firing position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did people from the crew at that position tell you that Zoran Primic had gone to get the shells, driving in a white Golf Kedi vehicle?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a passenger vehicle. I don't know which kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So up to 11.00, when you came to visit the SDK position, all the mortars were out of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After 11.30.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after 11.30, all the SDK mortars were out of ammunition?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where did the shooting come from after 11.30?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Babin Kuk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mortars by the SDK building, were they the ones that fired the four shells referred to?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether they were actually shooting after 11.30 on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably in order to fire those four shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're only making an assumption?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the auto camp Solitudo? How many shells were fired from the mortar position there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said already a few minutes ago that I don't know, that I Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. can't remember how many shells were fired from each and every firing position, because that's what the situation was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: And the mortars from the Solitudo camp, where were they firing at?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The slopes of Srdj and the fort of Srdj and partly towards Strincjera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they target Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, but probably yes. On two or three occasions, with the 120-millimetre mortar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about cannons from Babin Kuk? Did they fire at Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no cannon at Babin Kuk. The other cannon was at Mala Petka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was fired at from Mala Petka?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the area of Podbrezje, four shells. So that is the north-western area when viewed from Dubrovnik. I remember that because we had to transfer all the ammunition from that combat position to the firing position I already referred to, underneath the bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us conclude, Mr. Negodic. Is it correct that you cannot give me an answer about the number of fired shells from your artillery pieces on the 6th of December, 1991, except for the information provided for the ZIS cannon by the Ivo Vojnovic Street?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in part, sir, because I know about two cannons and the rocket launcher and the firing position that was not actually firing. So there were only two more combat positions for mortars that I cannot give you any answers about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there were only two remaining combat positions for mortars that were very important for your defence on the 6th of December, how come you cannot remember, or how come you will not remember?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you've started putting some very strange questions. Sir, I've already told you that I was in hospital for two or three days, and I came when the commander had already talked to the commanding officers of particular units. I was spared, if I can put it that way, any big discussions. So I did not know what the quantity of ammunition was for those two combat positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that mortars are unstable on a hard surface; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me: Can -- do mortars move when fired, when they are on your positions?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that mortars are moved -- mortars move all the time and that once a shell is fired, equipment has to be used for correcting fire yet again?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily, especially if targeting an area only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any precise targeting without sights?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on a mortar, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, paragraph 30 -- so paragraph 39, actually, you say: "I know that there were no heavy weapons in the Old Town." And in the last sentence of that paragraph, you say: "I only ever saw sidearms in the Old Town, never heavy weapons." When was it that you were in the Old Town? When did you have occasion to see sidearms only and you managed to see for yourself that there were no heavy weapons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that in November and December I was not in the Old Town at all, only on the 6th of December. I don't know what the translation was, but all indicators showed that when we would have a meeting at headquarters - and that is what I stated too - I never heard, or no one ever heard or saw that there were any heavy weapons within the walls, and that it was only refugees who brought hunting guns with them, and possibly pistols.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it that you saw this, Mr. Negodic?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it was not worded properly. "I saw." Perhaps it should have said "I heard." But anyway. I knew that there were no heavy weapons because this was under my command, and I knew where things were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's cut this short, Mr. Negodic. I'm going to read this out to you: "I only ever saw sidearms in the Old Town." What does "ever" mean? You actually said every time.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is plural, but it was not a question addressed as far as November and December are concerned in particular. It was a general question. So my answer was that every time I was in town, I could only notice this or that. But this is valid also for the month of January and also for before November and December. I already stated here yesterday that I was there for the first time on the 6th of December, when the Old Town was on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see only sidearms then too, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, that was during the night. We came for a different reason; to see if we could do anything to help extinguish the fire. We were not watching people who had rifles or whatever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm interested in knowing when it was that you saw only sidearms in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now you're asking me when. You want me to give a date or something. That is after the 6th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So until the 6th of December, 1991, you did not see anyone in the Old Town with sidearms?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not see anyone or anything when I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear of anyone moving about with sidearms in the Old Town until the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police provided information to that effect, that individuals were creating small problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these small problems have to do with weapons?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not any big weapons. Shotguns. So that was during brawls or things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, shotguns.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 24 of your statement, you said that: "At around 8.00, the position at Srdj came under combined arms attacks with infantry attacks. We provided fire support for the troops in Srdj as well as at the observation post and at JNA positions in Zarkovica." Were these the two basic directions in which your artillery operated, including your mortars, on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the most part, were shells fired at those two positions, namely, Srdj and Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Except for these two positions, did your forces shoot at any other positions on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me briefly which ones?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Strincjera, the north-western approaches to Dubrovnik, namely, Sustjepan. And as I've already said, four rockets in the Podbrezje area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also say Sustjepan?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Sustjepan, the approaches towards Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be given Exhibit P61, tab 30. That is from Mr. Hvalkof's tab.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, there is a document before you which is a Prosecution exhibit in this case, and it is a diary, a log sheet, rather, of a member of the monitoring mission, the deputy head of the office in Split, Mr. Per Hvalkof. Could you please read the first item pertaining to the time of 6.00 a.m. on December...

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to read that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Shelling from land and sea towards the fortress close to the TV tower and the harbour commenced."

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not know what the relevance Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. is in showing an exhibit, Prosecution exhibit tendered through another witness to this particular witness, unless this witness could comment on this document, unless he's familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The object, I'd have thought, was fairly clear, Ms. Mahindaratne. The witness has given some considerable evidence about what his artillery positions fired at that day, and when. And now the log of a European Community observer of that same day's operations is being put to him. We may find there are similarities or there may be differences. We will see. Carry on, Mr. Rodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Negodic, I have told you what kind of document this is, and you saw what it says for the 6th of December at 6:00 a.m. Do the monitors establish, inter alia, that fire was opened, or rather, that shelling commenced from land and sea?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which part of the sea do they mean? Perhaps Zupska Uvala, where they were anchored, as I already said, but there were no attacks from sea in the town, in the narrow sense of the word, as we already said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what it says here is Srdj.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, shelling, yes, Srdj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Shelling, Srdj?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it say shelling from land and sea?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that morning, was there any shelling from sea?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area of town, or rather, Srdj, in my opinion, was not on the 6th of December against Dubrovnik. I mean, there wasn't any shelling coming from the sea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you on that morning, if you remember, at 6.00?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At headquarters, at the Zagreb Hotel, in the area of Lapad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this information doesn't seem to be right. It doesn't seem to be truthful.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, saying from the sea would not be right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We no longer need this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: When you spoke about preparing the landing in Kupari, you said that a day before the landing, artillery preparations were carried out at the Rijeka Dubrovacka and Brgat, and that the JNA opened fire from Konavle with far-range artillery; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A day before the landing, I said that in the area of Zupa Dubrovacka and Brgat, this took place. There was no need to involve Rijeka Dubrovacka, which is on the opposite side. This was artillery preparation before the landing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Tell me: Did the JNA open fire then in October when preparing this landing from the area of Konavle too by using long-range artillery?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly it came from the area of Herzegovina, and we assume that multiple rocket launchers were used from the area of Konavle, against the area of Konavle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Cilipi?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cilipi near the airport.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The position by the airport?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they operating from there?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot tell you anything sure for that particular time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to the best of your knowledge, on the 6th of December, 1991, the Croatian forces only had wounded soldiers? I'm talking about soldiers.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am only talking about artillery, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me: Regarding the 6th of December, do you know when the attack started, when the JNA attack started?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already stated that this was in the early morning hours. It was not night-time. It was in the early morning hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was a winter day, so, say at 6.30, when it dawns.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see this, hear this? Were you informed about it?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I heard about it and then I saw it too. I heard about it at the command post, and then I was given orders to go out to the place that I already mentioned, I already said where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Negodic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RODIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, following your instructions, I have tailored my questions for today and I have thus concluded my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Rodic, thank you very much indeed for that effort. Clearly, you kept your eye clearly on the target and the time, and we've achieved what was desirable. I think that will make this a convenient time for the first morning break, and we will be having the second morning break a little earlier than usual. Apparently that will coincide with a time for a short medical examination of your client. We'll adjourn now for the first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne. Can we take it that you are likely to finish in this session your re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I hope I could, Your Honours. If it was one and a half hours, yes, I certainly would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It won't be that. We'll need to break just after 12.00. We will still live in hope that you'll manage to finish in that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'll try my very best, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May the two maps P159 and 160 be shown to the witness, the two maps that were marked by the Prosecution in the course of examination-in-chief. And while it's being done, I'll ask some questions from Mr. Negodic. Re-examined by Ms. Mahindaratne:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Negodic.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you were questioned in the course of cross-examination as to if 82-millimetre mortars could be considered as infantry weapons, and you agreed with that proposition. Now, were 82-millimetres mortars belonging to the Dubrovnik force under your control during the period 1st October 1991 to 31st December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you know if the infantry positions which were -- and I'm referring to your infantry positions, the Croatian infantry positions, had any 82-millimetre mortars, and especially in relation to map 160, if you could indicate that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Could Madam Usher perhaps show the witness the big map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, there are -- your infantry lines are indicated with the orange short lines. Were there any 82-millimetre mortars at those positions?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if any other person other than yourself belonging to the Dubrovnik defence force had 82-millimetre mortars under his or her control?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. While the map is before you, sir, could you make a correction. And I'm referring, Your Honours, to the correction I pointed out yesterday. The Maljutka position at position near Hotel President in Lapad, could you mark it with a "D." At the moment the marking is "B." Can you convert that to a "D," please. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now in the course of cross-examination, sir, when you were questioned with regard to the legend in this map which is placed before you, you stated that the map did not reflect the ground situation as at 6 December, and you even went on to say that that was the case even with regard to the other map, which is the smaller one, numbered with P359 [sic]. Now, when I questioned you in Court the previous day - sir, permit me to finish my question - you made certain amendments to these maps. If you take this particular map before you. You drew squares around two positions, marked "B" and "C" and indicated that those positions were not there on 6 December 1991. Isn't that the case, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you included three positions. Near Mala Petka you put a cross and indicated that the position depicted within the square marked with "C" was in fact at this new position marked with a cross and "C"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also indicated where the rocket launcher was on 6 December 1991, which was at -- close to Hotel Libertas, which is now marked on this map with a cross and "A"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you also indicated where the Maljutka was on the 6th of December, 1991, which was at Hotel President in Lapad, which you marked with a cross and now it's depicted with the letter "D"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Subject to these amendments, sir, would you say as to whether the ground situation with regard to artillery, mortars, and anti-aircraft weapons reflects the ground situation as at 6 December on this map, subject to those amendments?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With the corrections made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And likewise, sir, in the other map too, you made certain amendments. You indicated three positions with squares as not being there on 6 December 1991 and two positions with circles as being there on 6 December 1991. Subject those amendments, do the positions in map bearing Prosecution number P159 reflect the ground situation as at 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you said, in response to the Defence -- learned Defence counsel's question that these maps did not reflect the ground situation as at 6 December 1991, what you meant was prior to those amendments, the situation did not reflect the ground situation. Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that situation has now been corrected with your own amendments?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In reference to map bearing P160, do the other symbols, that is, the symbols that indicate the shelters and the mines and the infantry lines, do they reflect the ground situation as at 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be sure about the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking for the details. Would you be able to give a general idea as to whether the other -- you don't have to go through each and every -- perhaps I will withdraw that question, Your Honour. With regard to the legend on this bigger map, P160, at the top left-hand corner of the map, does it -- and I will rephrase the word. It's not the legend, it's a chart indicated at the top left-hand corner. Does it reflect the situation as at 6 December 1991? I'm referring to that chart at the top left-hand corner, sir.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was drawn by operative workers, and they probably did it based on the information from scout groups regarding firing positions and observation posts in the area of the map that you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, sir. My question to you is: The chart at the top left-hand corner. I'm referring to the chart. Could you just place your point on the chart. No, sir. Top right-hand corner. I'm sorry. I got my sides wrong. Beg your pardon, Your Honour. Does that reflect the situation as at 6 December 1991?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the details, because this encompasses the infantry and the navy and everything, if you're asking me about the artillery, I can answer that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will not go into those details now, Mr. Negodic. Thank you. In reference to a question with regard to that chart, you stated that you had not used this particular map in the Dubrovnik defence headquarters, and you went on to say that it was because this legend indicated that the map would have been used at the level of the commanders of the town defence. In stating that, was it your position that you had not used this map with this particular chart or was it your position that this is not a headquarters map of the Dubrovnik defence? I ask that, sir, because in examination-in-chief, you did identify this map as a headquarters map.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the map of the commander of the city defence, and there was no need for me to work with this map. I had my own map, with only my firing positions drawn in, and the targeted sector.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this map is in fact a Dubrovnik defence headquarters map?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Although it was not signed by the commander, Nojko Marinovic; it was signed by Mirko Katanic instead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, while we are -- no. I withdraw that. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me a brief explanation. This overview was typed above the signature of General Nojko Marinovic. I would like to confirm it, but otherwise I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you're saying, sir, is that the chart has been superimposed on the map and if that chart on the top right-hand corner was not there, one would be able to see the signature of General Marinovic? Is that what you just indicated?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Negodic, when you were questioned about the anti-aircraft weapon position depicted in this map to the north of the Old Town, you said the position was by a cable-car. Now, could you indicate with your pointer where the cable-car would be.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that also the position where the head of that symbol, the weapons symbol, is?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is a little further to the right and above.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to your knowledge of the ground situation, is it according to your knowledge of the ground situation that you said that generally this weapon was located at the cable-car, to the north of the Old Town? Is it on the basis of your knowledge that you said so?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the meeting of their command, when the air defence commander got the floor, he said that he would place there an anti-aircraft weapon, either Igla or Strela 2-M, and to the right, one of these two weapons, so that he would have an alternative position to the west of the Old Town for the area of Gradac. That's what I stated and that is a fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that meeting, sir?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you approximately give the distance between the cable-car, the location where the anti-aircraft weapon was generally positioned, to the walls of the Old Town? What was approximately the distance?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think 130 or 150 metres perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You were cross-examined about your response given in the course of examination-in-chief with regard to positioning of weapons and in the context of symbols. That is your response that in the case of anti-aircraft weapons, the position is indicated at the head of the symbol, as opposed to the symbol depicting mortar weapons, where the position is generally at the middle. Now, it was put to you that there were no military rules which governed this. Was your response based on the general practice utilised in map drawing or was it based on some military rules? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operative staff, as I already stated a couple of times, charted the maps, and as you can see, and as I responded to questions from the Defence, when you look at this firing position we are discussing now, and when we go east of this firing position to another firing position, it is evident that the exact place of this mortar position directly by the sea is not drawn in. I suppose the operative staff member also failed to indicate the top of that marking --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if I may interrupt you. My question was: Was your response based on general practices involved in map drawing or was it based on a military rule? That was my question. When you said about positioning of weapons and indication thereof by symbols, were you referring to general map drawing practices or were you referring to military rules? Which of these? For example, your indication that in the case of mortars, the position is at the middle of the symbol. Was it based on general map drawing practice or was it based on military rules? That was my question. If you could respond briefly which of these two.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the prevailing practice. I said we should draw mortars that way, and that's the way mortars are drawn, and as far as air defence weapons are concerned, I think they are indicated by the tip of the arrow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, you just said so also and you said even in the course of cross-examination, that the mortar position to the east of this anti-aircraft weapon we just discussed about is not exactly where it should be. Could you with your pointer indicate where exactly it should be. And if I may have the assistance of Madam Usher to -- no. I think the area is on the -- shown on the ELMO. Where exactly should that position be?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give an indication in terms of distance to -- and the direction to the position where it is now indicated.

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you are pointing to a position to the south of where the position is depicted. And in terms of distance, can you give approximately how much it is?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This firing position was drawn in, as far as I can see, 50 or 70 metres above the firing position, which was in place on the 6th of December. So it should go down to be below the road, because it was 15 to 20 metres away from the sea, in the park, actually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you're saying is that position should in fact be below the position where it is indicated, closer to the coastal line?

utterances.speaker: IVAN NEGODIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also questioned on the differences in the symbols indicating anti-aircraft weapons. Notwithstanding the symbols, because you were extensively examined on certain differences in dots, et cetera, are you in a position to state that the weapons positioned you indicated to be anti-aircraft weapons were in fact anti-aircraft weapons and not mortar or artillery positions? And I'm referring to the four positions, anti-aircraft positions that you indicated on this map. Do you understand my question, sir?
