But if the Defence wishes that a copy -- or if the Chamber wishes to have the entire document, which is lengthy, we're happy to do so. I think that for purposes of relevance and authenticity, we would be on solid ground to ask for the admission of this portion of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I leave it to counsel to discuss what parts of the document are relevant to this case, and could we expect agreement between counsel for those parts to be extracted and then tendered? So we'll wait for that agreement and that tendering. I think if each of you want a particular part of the document, we should be able to get that. It seems far more practical than to have a document of nearly 200 pages, of which only one or two pages is of relevance.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It is my understanding, Your Honour, that the entire document has been disclosed to the Defence, and so if perhaps by tomorrow morning we might be able to hear from them as to what parts, we're perfectly happy to have those sections in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. We will reach an agreement, I believe, very easily regarding this document and the other one as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As in all matters, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, Your Honour, certain things do not lend themselves to agreements until the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would like to ask you, please, to turn your attention to the part of this document -- well, if I can ask for an exhibit number, an identification number, it would be helpful and I'll refer to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will receive what comes to be agreed under an exhibit number which will now be given by the court officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at what has been identified or marked for identification as P162, I'd like to ask you to look -- I'll refer principally to the English, but the pages numbers are the same from translation purposes, or for translation purposes, in Croatian. If you look at page 1, page 1, in English - at the top is L0095757 - do you see a reference, at the time of 8.15, to the Argosy II? Do you see a reference there? Yes.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you -- would you be kind enough just to indicate what the reference -- what that particular entry says about the Argosy II. What was the Argosy II with reference or with respect to what you were doing in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF
utterances.text: What it says here is that Argosy II set out at 8.15. That was the ship we used to travel to Cavtat for negotiations with JNA representatives. This is authentic, I believe. It says that the ship also carried EC representatives, but we were there as well. It was -- there was a discussion with the captain about the flag, that it should be white or blue. And indeed, we took this ship to travel to Cavtat. There were two ships, actually, Argosy I and Argosy II, and we will probably have more occasion to discuss them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had this ship been a ship that was used in the Dubrovnik area for both official functions for the monitors, as well as for other functions? Do you know? Was it -- what was the purpose of this particular ship?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was used --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... to look at page 10 of P162 and take a look at the entry for 10.00. Again, the entry indicates: "We ask you to grant the Argosy II free passage on Monday, 9 December 1991 to provide Cavtat with food and medicines," et cetera, et cetera. Is that the same vessel, the Argosy II, that you were travelling on, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF
utterances.text: Look, page 10, I don't see that text on page 10. And anyway, I don't know these details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Yes. It says -- it says under the --

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF
utterances.text: Yes. It says "European Mission." Page 10, you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In English it is page 10.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF
utterances.text: Is this the English version? I'm looking at the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... probably a bit easier in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm afraid you have numbers at the top which are 3, and at the bottom which are 10. You're successfully confusing --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- many of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I apologise. I'm looking at the bottom one. I apologise to all of you. I'm sort of fixed on the --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes. That's the ERN, but the actual page number, I apologise to all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm trying to help the court officer find the page for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Right. At the bottom there will be a page 10. I'm sorry to Mr. Rudolf as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see it now, Mr. Rudolf? Do you see the entry that I just mentioned, where it talks about the -- asking to grant the Argosy II --

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. But that is the 9th of December, when the agreement came into force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question to you, however, is -- at this point we're not talking about an agreement, but just an entry in this particular log which refers to the Argosy II for transportation of food and medicines. Is that the same Argosy II?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF
utterances.text: I don't know, because both ships, Argosy I and Argosy II, were sunk on the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is on the 5th -- this is an entry for the 5th of December.

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF
utterances.text: There were two, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This entry is on the 5th. It talks about a future for the 9th. Talking -- it's written on the 5th, but it talks about the 9th. A future use of -- a future use. Is that the same Argosy II?

utterances.speaker: DAVORIN RUDOLF
utterances.text: In that case, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Speakers are overlapping.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I realise we're out of time for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, you are, Ms. Somers, and we must, I'm afraid, call an end to today's hearing because the next session --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- will start soon. Now, I'm afraid, Dr. Rudolf, that we are going to be not as easy to fit in with as we would like to be tomorrow and Thursday. Some time ago we arranged special hearings for tomorrow and Thursday. We have videolink evidence coming in from the United States, in particular, tomorrow morning. We commence sitting at 8.00 to receive that. And at 10.00 tomorrow morning we have your ambassador from Croatia coming to put submissions to us about an aspect of the case. That means that tomorrow we will not be able to continue with your evidence until sometime between 10.45 and 11.00. Unfortunately, tomorrow we must also finish at about 12.20, which means it will be a short session and your evidence will certainly not finish. We're sorry for that inconvenience, but these things had been arranged some time ago. And the pattern will be somewhat similar on the day following, Thursday. We hope somehow out of all of this that we will manage to conclude your evidence as quickly as possible and as coherently as possible. We will adjourn now, to resume tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
